subject: EHR exports + audit log identifiers — BAA coverage and logging guidance
messages:
From: Julie Miller <julie.miller@healthbridge.co>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@healthbridge.co>, Kevin Santos <kevin.santos@ehrvendor.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: scheduled EHR extracts + audit logs under BAA?

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving into technical design and had a couple of architecture questions that affect BAA scope:

1) We plan to schedule nightly batch EHR exports (CSV) from our EHR to a customer-controlled SFTP endpoint. Redwood will process those files to produce de-identified summaries and a small per-row token that links back to our internal patient id (a one-way hash). Will the presence of those hashes in Redwood-generated audit logs / job traces be considered PHI under the BAA, or can we treat them as non-PHI if they are cryptographic hashes?

2) For on-demand clinician voice notes we plan to send audio via webhook to Redwood for transcription. Transcripts will be written back to our system. Are intermediate transcripts or partial tokens retained in logs or tracing, and does that count as storage of PHI?

We need answers to these to finalize the security design and retention settings. If possible, a short summary we can include in our vendor review would be great.

Appreciate your help —
Julie Miller
Director, Vendor Integrations
HealthBridge Medical

Attachments: example_export_row.csv (sample row), current_integration_diagram.png
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Julie Miller <julie.miller@healthbridge.co>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: scheduled EHR extracts + audit logs under BAA?

Hi Julie —

Thanks — good, detailed questions. Short answers up front:
- Hashes that can be mapped back to an identifiable person by you (HealthBridge) are treated as PHI under our BAA unless they are transformed with irreversible tokenization we manage and the customer cannot reverse.
- Transcripts or partial transcripts that flow through our service and are stored in logs/traces are considered PHI if they contain identifiers or content that could identify a patient.

That said, we have configuration options and architecture patterns to keep your audit/tracing lightweight and outside PHI scope. I’ve looped in Stephanie (security sales) and Monica (solutions) to propose concrete options and propose changes to the BAA language if needed.

Next steps: Stephanie/Monica — can you propose a minimal-logging pattern for (a) scheduled SFTP batch processing that keeps the row-level hash out of logs and (b) webhook transcription so intermediate artifacts aren’t persisted? Also, include any required BAA wording changes or a short addendum.

I’ll also attach our suggested scope form and a log-field catalog for reference.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed design notes for HealthBridge — minimal PHI exposure

Dylan / team —

Notes on both items (high level):

1) Scheduled EHR exports (SFTP -> Redwood):
- Ingest pipeline: we can accept the CSV into an isolated ingest buffer that is processed on a dedicated worker pool. The default behavior writes a job-level metadata record (job_id, timestamp, row_count) but does NOT include per-row fields unless the customer opts-in.
- Hash handling: we recommend you (HealthBridge) send a truncated/salted hash (best) or we run a one-way tokenization step that stores only a non-reversible token in our database. If you keep your original mapping internally and we never store the mapping, the token alone is still PHI under the BAA if the token is reversible by you; therefore to minimize BAA footprint we prefer the customer-supplied truncated-salt approach or server-side irreversible tokenization that we attest to.
- Logging: we can add a config flag (redact_row_keys=true) — when set, all logs and traces will only reference the job_id and row index (e.g., job_id=HB-3321-20270629, row_index=42), but no patient_id/hash field will be logged. See attached log-field-catalog.csv for fields that are logged by default.

2) Webhook transcription (on-demand audio):
- Live path: transcripts are created in-memory and returned to your webhook endpoint. By default we retain a short ephemeral transcript cache (TTL 1 hour) for retry/DR; we can reduce TTL to 0 (no persistence) or zero-logging mode for PHI traffic.
- Debugging and evals: if you want quality monitoring, we can route a separate opt-in stream to an evaluation queue that is covered under the BAA. That queue stores de-identified examples only after you approve redaction rules.

Legal / BAA language: we’ll need an explicit clause that covers logged artifacts (job metadata, transient cache) and confirms whether tokens/hashes are treated as PHI. I can spin a short addendum.

I’m attaching a proposed diff of BAA language and the log-field catalog.

—Stephanie
Senior Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Julie Miller <julie.miller@healthbridge.co>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposed design notes for HealthBridge — minimal PHI exposure

Julie / Amanda —

Following up with concrete language and attachments. Quick summary for your vendor review:
- Redwood will treat any identifier (including deterministic hashes) as PHI unless the identifier is rendered non-reversible and the customer cannot map it back (e.g., irreversible tokenization performed by Redwood with no mapping stored, or customer-supplied truncated salted hash agreed in writing).
- By default Redwood stores only job-level metadata and will not log per-row identifiers unless redact_row_keys=false. We recommend setting redact_row_keys=true for your Nightly export job.
- For webhook transcriptions, set transcription_persistence=none to avoid any storage of transcripts. We can enable ephemeral retries without persistence if you prefer.

Attached: proposed-baa-language-diff.txt (short addendum you can include in procurement), log-field-catalog.csv. I’ve also attached the completed HB-BAA-scope-form.pdf that our procurement requests to start a BAA. Please sign and return and we’ll route to Legal.

Next step: Julie/Amanda — please confirm desired flags (redact_row_keys=true, transcription_persistence=none) and return the scope form. Happy to join a short call to finalize.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Julie Miller <julie.miller@healthbridge.co>, Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@healthbridge.co>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EHR exports + audit log identifiers — BAA coverage and logging guidance

Julie / Amanda —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. To make procurement simple, here are the confirmed recommendations and next steps we’ll include in the BAA addendum:

1) Nightly batch EHR exports: set redact_row_keys=true (default for HealthBridge). Redwood will only log job-level metadata (job_id, start/end, row_count, error_count). No per-row identifiers or hashed patient IDs will be written to logs or tracing systems. If you require per-row debugging, that must be explicitly enabled and will be captured under the BAA.

2) Webhook transcription: set transcription_persistence=none. Transcripts will be streamed back to your webhook and held only transiently for retries (TTL 1 minute) with no persistence in our audit logs. Any sampling for quality monitoring will be opt-in and de-identified per your approval.

3) Tokenization guidance: If you supply deterministic hashes that you can reverse, Redwood will consider them PHI. If you require minimal BAA footprint, either supply truncated salted hashes or opt into Redwood irreversible tokenization (no mapping retained). We will include explicit language in the addendum stating that reversible tokens supplied by the customer are treated as PHI.

4) Attachments / evidence: I’ve attached the HB-BAA-scope-form.pdf for signature and the small log-field catalog; Aditya attached the BAA diff for procurement.

Please confirm the two config flags and return the signed scope form. If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with our security engineer to walk the infra tweaks.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
